investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official '/agenda/' listing page and one linked event detail page. Both are plain server-rendered WordPress HTML; every event is a static <article class="evenement-item"> card carrying a machine-readable <time datetime=...> attribute, a title, and a room name, with no schema.org Event JSON-LD anywhere (only generic Yoast SEO WebPage/Organization JSON-LD).

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.lamachinedumoulinrouge.com/agenda/ immediately exposed 42 static event cards (<article class="evenement-item ...">), each with a machine-readable <time datetime="2026-08-28T23:59:00+00:00">, a title (h2.titevtagenda), a room name (div#lieuevtagenda), and its own canonical event URL — no escalation needed. A second plain GET of one linked detail page (chronologic-2) confirmed the same title/date/room directly and additionally exposed an explicit end time ('23H59 — 06H00').

venue_reference: La Machine du Moulin Rouge (club/concert venue, 90 Boulevard de Clichy, 75018 Paris — a distinct venue adjacent to, and NOT part of, the Moulin Rouge cabaret itself)

identity.notes: Retained page's own <title> reads 'Agenda | La Machine du Moulin Rouge | clubs ∙ concerts ∙ expos ...' at the venue's own domain lamachinedumoulinrouge.com (generator meta tag: WordPress 7.1). The sitewide footer states '90 bd de Clichy / 75018 Paris', matching the venue's known address, and every asset URL is self-hosted under wp-content/uploads/. This domain/branding is explicitly distinct from moulinrouge.fr (the cabaret) — confirmed by the retained page's own branding, address, and content (club/concert/exhibition programming, not a cabaret revue) never referencing the cabaret as the same entity.

site_classification.platform: WordPress 7.1 (generator meta tag present; a single generic Yoast-style WebPage/WebSite JSON-LD block is present but contains no schema.org Event data). Every event is rendered as a plain static HTML <article> card on one listing page, with a matching detail page per event.

title.notes: The h2.titevtagenda text on the listing card, confirmed identical on the event's own detail page heading.

start_date.notes: The card's own <time datetime="2026-08-28T23:59:00+00:00"> date portion, confirmed by the same page's own human-readable badge ('Ven 28/08') and the detail page's own badge ('Ven 28/08').

time.notes: IMPORTANT HONESTY CAVEAT, found and retained during this investigation: the machine-readable <time datetime=...> attribute's trailing '+00:00' is NOT evidence of a genuine UTC instant. Every one of the 42 sampled cards' datetime attributes carries the identical '+00:00' suffix regardless of calendar date, spanning a real Europe/Paris DST transition (late October 2026) — a genuine UTC conversion would show a mix of +02:00 (CEST, before the transition) and +01:00 (CET, after it), not a constant +00:00 in every case. This proves '+00:00' is a fixed placeholder appended by the site's theme/plugin, not a real timezone conversion — the same category of 'looks stable but isn't' finding already logged for Hot Clube de Portugal's ICS UID. The wall-clock digits themselves (23:59) are directly stated and corroborated by the page's own human-readable text ('23H59'), so time is recorded PROVEN/DIRECT_SOURCE for the wall-clock value only, with certainty FLOATING_LOCAL — never upgraded to a UTC instant.

end.value: 06:00, following calendar day (Europe/Paris floating local wall-clock)
end.notes: The event's own detail page directly states the time range '23H59 — 06H00' in its hero info block. Same floating-local caveat as 'time' above applies — this is a directly-stated wall-clock value, not a confirmed UTC instant.

venue_location.value: La Machine du Moulin Rouge — Central, 90 Boulevard de Clichy, 75018 Paris
venue_location.notes: Each event card and detail page directly states its own room name within the venue complex ('Central', 'Bar à Bulles', 'Chaufferie'), but the full venue name+street address is not repeated beside the event data itself. This is mechanically determinable: the site is a dedicated single-venue domain with no other venue ever named, and its sitewide footer states the full address identically on both sampled pages.

derivation.rule: every event card's own directly-stated room name identifies the specific space within this dedicated single-venue domain's own complex; concatenate that room name with the site's own sitewide footer address to get each event's full venue_location
inputs: event card/detail page directly states its own room name (e.g. 'Central') via div#lieuevtagenda
sitewide footer states '90 bd de Clichy / 75018 Paris' identically on the listing and detail page

source_record_id.notes: The event's own WordPress permalink slug ('/evenement/chronologic-2/'), used as this source's own canonical path — the same documented judgement as tempodrom-berlin-01/le-trabendo-paris-01. Empirically strengthened here: two distinct sampled events share the same title ('Chronologic', on 2026-08-28 and again on 2026-09-04) but resolve to two genuinely distinct slugs ('chronologic-2' and 'chronologic'), confirming the slug — not the title — is this source's real per-record identity.

event_url.notes: The card's own href, confirmed to resolve to the detail page sampled.

price.notes: No price is stated on either sampled page. Ticketing is delegated entirely to a third-party platform (shotgun.live) via an outbound 'Billetterie' link, matching the same pattern already found and bounded-checked (HTTP 429, not retried) for le-trabendo-paris-01 on the same third-party domain — not repeated here to avoid redundant third-party probing.
